source_signature.notes: Fluid pressure — equivalent resultant and line of action for hydrostatic loading on a submerged plane surface, authored to the Architect scope ruling with fluid dynamics excluded. This artifact was reviewed by FULL independent re-derivation because the packet transmission to Cursor truncated and the worked example was reconstructed rather than echoed from supplied data; every value was verified from scratch. Re-derived: gauge pressure p = rho g h zero at the free surface and rising linearly to p_bottom = rho g H = 1000 x 9.81 x 3 = 29430 Pa = 29.43 kPa at the base, giving a triangular distribution of height 3 m and base 29.43 kPa. The equivalent resultant per unit width equals the pressure-triangle area, R = (1/2)(29430)(3) = 44145 N/m = 44.145 kN/m, confirmed independently by the closed form R = (1/2) rho g H^2 = (1/2)(1000)(9.81)(9) = 44145 N/m, two routes to the same value, and R acts perpendicular to the gate. THE LINE-OF-ACTION POINT BITES, which is the whole reason hydrostatic loading is not a uniform-load problem: the resultant acts through the centroid of the triangular distribution at one-third the height from the bottom, h_R = (2/3) H = 2.0 m below the free surface, and the artifact explicitly rejects the mid-depth 1.5 m that a uniform load would give, presenting the 1.5-to-2.0 shift as the physical content — more load is concentrated deep where pressure is highest — with the sanity check h_R = 2.0 > 1.5 confirming the resultant acts below mid-depth. BOUNDARY to simple_distributed_load_resultant drawn cleanly in one sentence: that skill gives the general area-and-centroid rule for any loading curve, and this skill specializes it to the hydrostatic case where the curve is fixed by p = rho g h and is therefore triangular from the free surface; the general rule is applied-as-specialized, not re-derived, and the triangle one-third centroid is cited rather than re-derived by integration. Fluid dynamics is excluded explicitly — no velocity, Bernoulli, or dynamic pressure — along with buoyancy-of-floating-body and surface sizing. Two earned signals at distinct steps: sign_or_placement_error at step 4 where the line of action is located and placing it at mid-depth is the failure, and unclassified at step 1 as the boundary fallback covering fluid dynamics, uniform-pressure treatment, re-deriving the general rule, and sizing. THE simple_average_used DISPOSITION IS ARGUED CORRECTLY: averaging top and bottom pressure to invent a mid-depth line of action is the same wrong placement already covered by sign_or_placement_error at step 4, not a separate Centroids-family averaging error, so it is not double-mapped — the correct reading of simple_average_used as coordinate averaging without area weighting rather than any average anywhere. axis_confusion and solution_sequencing_error cannot be earned: no axis-pair choice or transform, and no stranded phase order. Honest limitation recorded: the one-third rule and the closed form (1/2) rho g H^2 hold only for the free-surface triangular case, a submerged-top surface being trapezoidal with a differently located centroid, and the result is per unit width for a static fluid on a rigid fixed surface. Symbol discipline: R reused with the resultant framing from simple_distributed_load_resultant, hydrostatic-specific rho, g, h, H, p, p_bottom and h_R introduced distinctly, and no binding of u, d, k, I, M_O, theta, A_gen or V. Fourth skill of Batch 4N, third in a newly created subtopic; signed from its re-parented FLUID_PRESSURE location; required no correction, though it required full re-derivation rather than a fingerprint match owing to the transmission truncation.
